dismissals.because: src/forge/close.py:220 a file git ignores is never committed, so it never reaches the pull request and can't leave the upgrade's committed files stale; the check compares what the pull request carries

findings.body: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` omits ignored files. If the pinned release adds a generated path that the client ignores, `forge sync` writes it in the temporary worktree, but `stale` remains empty and close can report Ready without that file in the pull request. `src/forge/sync.py:264-275` writes generated paths whether Git ignores them. Compare the generated paths with the committed tree explicitly.
findings.title: Not done: An upgrade is not ready while synced files are out of date

findings.body: Running the full `forge sync` command also calls `install_shims` (`src/forge/sync.py:322`). Its hooks live in the Git hooks directory shared by all worktrees (`src/forge/githooks.py:46-50`), and installation can rewrite or rename them (`src/forge/sync.py:278-307`). A close that subsequently refuses a stale upgrade can therefore change the real repository's hooks. Compare generated files in the temporary checkout without installing hooks.
findings.title: Keep the close comparison from rewriting shared Git hooks

findings.body: `mkdtemp()` creates a parent directory, but the cleanup removes only its `sync` worktree and branch. Every upgrade close leaves the empty parent directory behind. Remove it after the worktree cleanup.
findings.title: Remove the temporary parent directory after the sync check
